correctness.rationale: For each discordant edge, the two opposite updater contributions cancel the baseline and leave \(w_e(b_u+b_v)/(2nD)\). The cut identity \(C(\{u\})+C(\{v\})-C(\{u,v\})=2w_e(b_u+b_v)\) proves the necessary condition. Connected graph parity classifies preference assignments. Strictly positive rates on a finite connected graph imply almost-sure consensus with finite mean, enabling bounded martingale convergence; weighted degrees of bipartition classes agree; the first-flip law is geometric and sharp on one edge. Checked by 456 exact one-step configurations and 292 independent finite absorbing-chain solves. No finite experiment is used as a proof of the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: Exact necessity/sufficiency identifies the entire neutrality locus rather than a toy-graph coincidence. It supplies arbitrary positive symmetric contact weights, shows nonzero opposing preferences leave all fixation odds exactly neutral, and establishes an unbounded increase of initial polarized persistence without changing either consensus probability. This is a natural boundary for studying conflicting partisanship and finite-network dynamics, not just a restatement of \(h=0\) voter folklore.
